title.narrative: Building Resilient Value Chains and Food Security in Northern Ghana

description.narrative:
Impact: Food Security strengthened in rural Northern Ghana.
Outcome 1: Agricultural sector is strengthened through market linkages; Outcome 2: Farmers access to market, knowledge and employment through hubs; Outcome 3: Farmers use regenerative agricultural practices.
Warc is planning to establish 7 mega Trading Hubs over 3 years, each equipped with a central hub, two 100MT silos, bagged maize and soybean storage, and trucks for efficient transport between satellite and mega hubs. Supported by 4 satellite hubs per mega hub, this network will engage 600 farmers per hub (50% women and youth) with improved inputs, training, and market access. The mega hubs, equipped with container-based infrastructure, silos, storage facilities, and cold rooms, are enhancing the operational efficiency and inventory management. The satellite hubs aggregate produce and deliver it to the mega hubs, where it is distributed to downstream buyers.
Warc will purchase 54,000 MT in total of maize over three years (Y1 – 9,600 MT, Y2 20,400 MT and Y3 24,000 MT), injecting €21 million into the local economy and creating 147 direct full-time jobs, with a strong focus on gender inclusion. Warc aims to supply Koudijs, a subsidiary of the Dutch animal feed company De Heus, their key partner with 30,000 MT of maize over the next three years. This collaboration contributes to sustainable agriculture, rural development and long-term food security in Ghana.
